source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 901 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

(a) PD 901 was established by Ordinance No. 29252, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 22, 2014.

(b) This district is divided into Subdistrict 1, Subdistrict 2, and Subdistrict 3 as described in the subdistrict property descriptions (Exhibit 901B). (Ord. 29252)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 901 is established on property located on the northeast side of Beacon Street between Columbia Avenue and Alton Avenue. The size of PD 901 is approximately 0.856 acres. (Ord. 29252)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this district:

(1) BED AND BREAKFAST means a lodging facility containing fifteen or fewer guest rooms and one kitchen. This use may not have kitchens in the guest room. Amenities such as maids, laundry, concierge, meeting rooms, exercise rooms, pool, and business services (fax, Internet, voicemail, courier, etc.) and food and beverage service may only be provided to registered guests.

(2) ORIGINAL STRUCTURE means a building that was constructed on the property before January 1, 2000.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 29252)

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 901A: development/landscape plan.

(2) Exhibit 901B: subdistrict property descriptions. (Ord. 29252)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development/landscape plan (Exhibit 901A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development/landscape plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 29252)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Subdistrict 1. The following uses are the only main uses permitted and must be located on the same lot as an original structure:

(1) Agricultural uses.

-- Crop production.

(2) Commercial and business service uses.

-- Catering service. -- Custom business services.

(3) Institutional and community service uses.

-- Adult day care facility. -- Church. -- Convent or monastery. -- Library, art gallery, or museum.

(4) Lodging uses.

-- Bed and breakfast.

(5) Miscellaneous uses.

-- Temporary construction or sales office.

(6) Office uses.

-- Office.

(7) Recreation uses.

-- Public park, playground, or golf course.

(8) Residential uses.

-- Multifamily.

(9) Retail and personal service uses.

-- General merchandise or food store 3,500 square feet or less.

-- Nursery, garden shop, or plant sales. -- Personal service uses.

(10) Transportation uses.

-- Transit passenger shelter.

(11) Wholesale, distribution, and storage uses.

-- Recycling drop-off container. [SUP required if the requirements of Section 51A-4.213(11.2)(E) are not satisfied.] -- Recycling drop-off for special occasion collection. [SUP required if the requirements of Section 51A-4.213(11.3)(E) are not satisfied.]

(b) Subdistrict 2.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the D(A) Duplex District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the D(A) Duplex District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the D(A) Duplex District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the D(A) Duplex District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(2) The following main use is also permitted:

Lodging uses.

-- Bed and breakfast.

(3) The following main use is prohibited:

Institutional and community service uses.

-- Child-care facility.

(4) All uses must be located within an original structure.

(c) Subdistrict 3.

(1) The only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the D(A) Duplex District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the D(A) Duplex District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the D(A) Duplex District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the D(A) Duplex District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(2) The following main use is prohibited:

Institutional and community service uses.

-- Child-care facility.

(3) Surface parking is permitted only as an accessory use to a main use located in Subdistrict 1 or Subdistrict 2 and may not be used as special parking under Division 51A-4.320 by any use outside of this district. (Ord. 29252)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.107. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any tract in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 29252)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Subdistrict 1. The yard, lot, and space regulations for the CR Community Retail District apply.

(b) Subdistrict 2 and Subdistrict 3.

(1) Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the D(A) Duplex District apply.

(2) A six-foot open wrought iron fence is permitted within a required front yard in Subdistrict 3 in the location shown on the development/landscape plan. (Ord. 29252)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Required parking for a bed and breakfast use is one parking space for each guest room.

(c) For purposes of off-street parking, the Property is considered one lot.

(d) Parking spaces located along Beacon Street, in the locations shown on the development/landscape plan, may be counted towards the parking requirements for uses located in Subdistrict 1 or Subdistrict 2.

(e) Required parking is permitted within a required front yard. (Ord. 29252)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 29252)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Landscaping for surface parking must be provided in accordance with the development/landscape plan (Exhibit 901A).

(c) Plants must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 29252)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.112. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 29252)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.113. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) In general.

(1) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(2) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(b) Subdistrict 3.

(1) A minimum 36-foot visibility triangle is required at the intersection of Beacon Street and East Side Avenue and at Beacon Street and Alton Avenue, as shown on the development/landscape plan.

(2) Lighting for surface parking is limited to a maximum height of four feet. (Ord. 29252)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-901.114. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29252)
